balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Globant S.A.: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Globant S.A.: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Globant S.A.: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Globant S.A.: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

headcount.title: Headcount
headcount.content:
Total employees is Globant's full headcount; IT professionals is the billable-delivery subset (studio/project staff, excluding corporate functions).

For Globant S.A.: this is a staffing-based delivery model -- revenue growth with no matching headcount growth means utilization/pricing is doing the work; headcount declines (as in FY2025-FY2026) show the business absorbing a demand slowdown by cutting capacity rather than growing into it.

What to watch:

  • Headcount growth vs revenue growth (utilization and pricing trend)
  • IT professionals as a share of total employees (delivery vs overhead mix)
  • Sequential declines signalling bench/utilization pressure

geoMix.title: Revenue by geography
geoMix.content:
Revenue split across North America, Latin America and Europe, each as a percent of total revenue for the quarter.

For Globant S.A.: North America is the largest and highest-margin market and the most exposed to US corporate IT-spending cycles; Latin America and Europe diversify that exposure and reflect the company's nearshore/onshore delivery footprint.

What to watch:

  • North America share rising or falling (demand concentration)
  • Europe share trend (newer, smaller market -- growth here is a diversification signal)
  • Sum of the three segments vs 100% (a rest-of-world residual may exist but isn't charted)

customerConcentration.title: Customer concentration
customerConcentration.content:
Customers > $1m/yr is the count of accounts billing over $1 million annually; top customer % is the largest single client's share of total revenue.

For Globant S.A.: the qualitative analysis flags client concentration as a named risk -- a large consulting/outsourcing relationship can be cancelled or re-tendered with limited notice, so the top-customer share is a direct read on that risk, while the count of $1m+ accounts shows whether the client base is broadening or narrowing.

What to watch:

  • Top customer % rising (concentration risk building)
  • Count of $1m+ customers declining while revenue holds up (fewer, bigger bets)
  • A large drop in either metric around a known client loss

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Globant S.A.: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Globant S.A.: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Globant S.A.: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Globant S.A.: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Globant S.A.: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Globant S.A.: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
